original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Bounded immutable-circuit reuse of exact states in the unchanged PR6030 primary replay.
scope_change_reason: The current selected primary replay and pure literal-state boundary make the generic replay-runtime question concrete.
bottleneck_link: Avoid repeated pure native-state evaluation while retaining the complete existing consumer, bindings and comparisons.
stop_rule: Stop after the fixed 512-state experiment and five alternating full-workload pairs; publish the first measured improvement or a precise negative handoff.
evidence: Five alternating fresh-process pairs pass with identical source and implementation hashes, request counts and complete scientific stdout. Ranges overlap; a full-replay speedup is unestablished. Exact cache controls pass normally and under optimized Python. README records every sample; benchmark.py generates a complete source-bound receipt to an external path.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which cost-weighted work is eliminated by the repeated keys?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Exact evaluator-call reductions do not imply the same runtime reduction.
open_questions.first_step: Profile the unchanged gate-table primary and separate key, copying, gate and caller costs.
open_questions.blocked_by: No successful complete cost-weighted profile of this final wrapper is supplied.

open_questions.question: Does the source-bound timing pattern persist on another host?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A shared-host timing is not a platform-independent result.
open_questions.first_step: Run benchmark.py with the same sources and preserve every sample.

result_claim_type: Source-bound empirical performance finding, with exact finite cache conformance; no theorem or kappa improvement.
